questions_and_answers.question: How are price tags often written at grocery stores and fish stores?

answers.answer: With the unit (e.g., 100g) and the price (e.g., 500円)

questions_and_answers.question: How are the price tags showing '100g / 500円' read aloud?
How do you say 'beef that is 300 yen per 100 grams'?
What is the general pattern for stating a price per unit of merchandise?
How do you say '1 kg of the apples that are 300 yen'?
When you have been talking about a particular item, what can you drop (as discussed in Lesson 17)?
What does '100 guramu 500-en no' mean (without the merchandise name)?

answers.answer: the one that is 500 yen for 100 g

questions_and_answers.question: How do you say 'Please give me 200 g of the one that is 500 yen for 100 grams'?
What does 'Kore o 200 guramu kudasai' mean?

answers.answer: Please give me 200 g of this.
How much is 200 grams of this?

questions_and_answers.question: The expression for ordering an amount of a priced item is essentially what?

answers.answer: An expansion of the basic 'X o (amount) kudasai' pattern

articles.text:
2. How to say '500 yen per 100 grams'

At grocery stores, fish stores, etc., the price tags are often written in the following ways: a tag showing '100g' and '500円', which can also be written with Kanji numerals. Note: The tags are read as 100 guramu 500 yen.

When you refer to beef that is 300 yen per 100 grams, for example, you can say:

100 guramu 300-en no (gyuu)niku

This expression can be generalized into the following pattern:

Unit (100 g, 1 kg, etc.) price no merchandise

e.g. 100 guramu 500-en no gyuuniku    100 g of the beef that is 500 yen
     1 kiro 300-en no ringo           1 kg of the apples that are 300 yen

However, as we discussed in Lesson 17, when you have been talking about a particular item or when you choose one from among several, it is not necessary to say its name again. You can simply say:

100 guramu 500-en no    the one that is 500 yen for 100 g

When you want to order 200 g of the merchandise that is 500 yen for 100 grams, for example, you can use the following expression:

100 guramu 500-en no o 200 guramu kudasai.    Please give me 200 g of the one that is 500 yen for 100 g

You may have noticed that this expression is merely an expansion of what we discussed above. Compare the following:

Kore o 200 guramu kudasai.                       Please give me 200 g of this
100 guramu 500-en no o 200 guramu kudasai.       Please give me 200 g of the one that is 500 yen for 100 g
